body.p: I. Introduction

With the cancellation herein without prejudice of claim 4, claims 1-3 and 5-10 are pending in the present application. No new matter has been added. In view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks, it is respectfully submitted that all the pending claims are allowable, and reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Applicant notes with appreciation the acknowledgement of the claim for foreign priority and the indication that all certified copies of the priority documents have been received.
II. Objection to Claim 8
Claim 8 has been amended herein, thereby rendering the objection thereto moot, and withdrawal of the objection to claim 8 is therefore respectfully requested.
III. Rejection of Claims 1-3 and 5-10 Under 35 U.S.C. & 101

Claims 1-3 and 5-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as assertedly being directed to non-patentable subject matter. The claims, as amended herein without prejudice, are directed to vehicle control and therefore satisfy the requirements of 35 U.S.C. § 101. Withdrawal of the rejection of claims 1-3 and 5-10 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 is therefore respectfully requested.
IV. Rejection of Claims 1, 3, and 8-10 Under 35 U.S.C. & 102

Claims 1, 3, and 8-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as anticipated by U.S. Pat. App. Pub. No. 2020/0180605 ("Boecker"). Boecker does not anticipate any of the present claims, and the rejection be withdrawn, for at least the following reasons.

Independent claims 1, 9, and 10 have been amended herein without prejudice to incorporate the subject matter of claims 2 and 4, with clarifying details. The Office Action asserts that U.S. Pat. App. Pub. No. 2018/0178769 ("Raste") suggests to use a target that is different than a setpoint direction and a steering direction. However, Raste concerns determining what direction a driver is actually intending to demand. Raste recognizes that a driver might slightly incorrectly move the steering wheel to a particular steering angle which corresponds to a setting of the vehicle in a particular direction that is slightly offset from the actual direction the driver intended. Raste's system can determine, based on a combination of the steering angle to which the driver set the steering wheel and the driving lane on which the vehicle is being driven what the driver's actual

intended direction demand is. Then, if it is determined based on current dynamics that the vehicle's travel direction will be different than the driver's determined intended direction, the system performs a corrective action. However, if the driver's steering is clearly different than any direction that might be expected from the driving lane, then there is no indication that the driving lane is used at all. Boecker describes a system where there is a desired autonomous driving trajectory and an actual trajectory, where the system constantly controls vehicle dynamics to remove any deviation, so that the desired trajectory is implemented.

Neither Boecker nor Raste suggests that where it is determined that a vehicle controller, e.g., a driver, is steering the vehicle in a manner indicating that the controller is intending to guide the vehicle in a direction different than a setpoint direction, then stabilization is performed to guide the vehicle in an altogether different direction than both of those directions.

Boecker (and Raste) therefore does not disclose or suggest all of the features of any of claims 1, 9, and 10, and therefore does not render unpatentable any of claims 1, 9, and 10 or either of claims 3 and 8, which depend from claim 1.
Withdrawal of the rejection of claims 1, 3, and 8-10 is therefore respectfully requested.
V. Rejection of Claim 2 Under 35 U.S.C. & 103

Claim 2 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over the combination of Boecker and Raste. Claim 2 depends from claim 1 and is therefore allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1. Withdrawal of the obviousness rejection of claim 2 is therefore respectfully requested.
VI. Rejection of Claim 5 Under 35 U.S.C. 4 103

Claim 5 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over the combination of Boecker and WO 2020/157798 ("Utsui"). Claim 5 depends from claim 1 and is therefore allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1 because Utsui does not correct the critical deficiencies of Boecker noted above as to claim 1. Withdrawal of the obviousness rejection of claim 5 is therefore respectfully requested.
VII. Rejection of Claims 6 and 7 Under 35 U.S.C. 4 103

Claims 6 and 7 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over the combination of Boecker and U.S. Pat. App. Pub. No. 2022/0281525 ("Ost"). Claims 6 and 7 depend from claim 1 and are therefore allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1 because Ost does not correct the critical deficiencies of Boecker noted above as to claim 1. Withdrawal of the obviousness rejection of claims 6 and 7 is therefore respectfully requested.
VIII. Conclusion

All issues raised having been addressed, it is therefore respectfully requested that the objection and rejections be withdrawn. Prompt reconsideration and allowance of the present application are therefore earnestly solicited.
Respectfully submitted, /Aaron Grunberger/
